content: The following is a professional summary of the declarations of interest and conflicts of interest for various contributors and experts involved in the Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) guidelines for mental, neurological, and substance use disorders: 1. Edwin Tan (University of Sydney, Australia), Vitor S. Tardelli (Centre for Addiction and Mental Health, University of Toronto, Canada, and Universidade Federal de São Paulo, Brazil), Alice Treloar (Australian Institute for Suicide Research and Prevention, Brisbane, Australia), Tracey Varker (Phoenix Australia, University of Melbourne, Australia), Simona Vecchi (University of Cagliari, Italy), Karen Watson (University of Sydney, Australia), and Stephanie Wong (Flinders University, Adelaide, Australia, and University of Sydney, Australia) declared no conflicts of interest. 2. Professor Sawitri Assanangkorchai and Professor Henry Brodaty (University of New South Wales, Sydney) also declared no conflicts of interest. However, Professor Brodaty disclosed consultancy and advisory board payments from Biogen Pharmaceuticals, Cranbrook Care, Nutricia Australia, Roche, and Skin2Neuron, as well as ongoing research support from Australia’s National Health Medical Research Council (NHMRC) and the Commonwealth Department of Health. These were not considered conflicts of interest. 3. Dr. Vladimir Carli (shareholder of Mental Health in Mind International AB), Dr. Odille Chang, Professor Pamela Y. Collins, Professor Pim Cuijpers, Professor Petrus J., and Professor Christopher Dowrick (unpaid chair of the World Organisation of Family Doctors Working Party for Mental Health, 2016–2021) declared no conflicts of interest. Professor Dowrick received research funding from the English National Institute for Health Research and the European Commission until 2020, which was not deemed a conflict. 4. Dr. Julian Eaton (employed by CBM Global and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine) disclosed unpaid involvement with several mental health networks and advisory groups, including the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) and the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN). No conflicts of interest were identified. 5. Dr. Rabih El Chammay, Professor Cleusa P. Ferri, Professor Sandra Fortes, Dr. Michael P. Hengartner, Dr. Asma Humayun, Dr. Maria Elena Medina-Mora, Professor Pratima Murthy, Professor Charles Newton, Professor Olayinka Omigbodun, Dr. Palmira Fortunato dos Santos, Professor Afarin Rahimi-Movaghar, Professor Shekhar Saxena, Ms. Charlene Sunkel (who withdrew from the GDG), Professor Wang Huali, Ms. Peach Wattanavitukul, and Ms. Enat Yewnetu declared no conflicts of interest. 6. Professor Atif Rahman (University of Liverpool, UK) disclosed technical advice provided to the Human Development Research Foundation and Shifa Tameer-e-Millat University, as well as research funding from the National Institute of Health Research (UK), National Institute of Mental Health (USA), and the Medical Research Council (UK). No conflicts of interest were identified. 7. Professor Sir Graham Thornicroft disclosed board memberships with United for Global Mental Health, Mental Health and Human Rights (F-GIP), and Implemental (formerly Maudsley International). He also received support from the NIHR Applied Research Collaboration South London and the NIHR Asset Global Health Unit award. These were not considered conflicts of interest. 8. Dr. Helal Uddin Ahmed, Professor Kaarin Anstey (ongoing research support from NHMRC for dementia risk assessment research), Dr. Lola Kola, Professor Crick Lund, Professor David Ndetei, Dr. Alfredo Pemjean, Professor Pratap Sharan, Dr. Vandad Sharifi Senejani, Dr. Gagandeep Singh (Chairperson of the International League Against Epilepsy Primary Care Task Force), Dr. David Shiers (honorary roles and minor payments for lectures and advisory work), Ms. Sahar Vasquez, and Professor Min Zhao declared no conflicts of interest. 9. Dr. Dinah Nadera disclosed consulting and training roles for CBM International and honoraria for speeches and training. These were not considered conflicts of interest. 10. Mr. Michael Njenga disclosed extensive work in human rights for persons with psychosocial disabilities and training roles for the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) since 2016. No conflicts of interest were identified.
